scope: Bootstrap RC.2 and security requirements for the MGK v0.1.0 candidate

findings.title: Gate-result subject is not validated or bound by check_gates
findings.description: check_gates requires subject only to be a string. It accepts an all-PASS document whose subject is neither a digest nor the patch/candidate identifier. make_attestation binds the final gate subject to the commit SHA but does not bind the pre-gate subject to PATCH_SHA256.
findings.impact: At the TCB API boundary, syntactically valid PASS evidence can be associated with the wrong subject. Current workflow artifact provenance reduces exploitability, but the attestation is not self-proving if evidence is supplied by another caller or the artifact boundary changes.

evidence.source_observation: make_attestation.py compares final_gates.subject with commit_sha but never compares pre_gates.subject with metadata.PATCH_SHA256

findings.recommended_regression: Make check_gates accept required_subject plus subject_format and compare exactly. In make_attestation call check_gates(pre, required_subject=PATCH_SHA256) and check_gates(final, required_subject=commit_sha).
findings.rationale: The frozen F00 workflow supplies artifacts from the same run and performs independent patch verification; this is a hardening defect, not a demonstrated F00 bypass. It must not be copied into the v0.1.0 evidence verifier.

findings.title: Candidate attestation is an unsigned JSON artifact
findings.description: The attestation contains hashes but has no detached signature or transparency-log inclusion. Its SHA-256 is placed in a PR body by the workflow.
findings.impact: After GitHub artifact retention expires or outside the authenticated run context, a consumer cannot establish provenance from the JSON alone.
findings.recommended_regression: For v0.1.0, bind manifest, verdict and evidence archive in a signed release statement or preserve them in an immutable provenance mechanism. At minimum verify all referenced hashes from the release archive.
findings.rationale: GitHub run identity and protected human merge provide bootstrap provenance; the standalone release requires stronger portable provenance.

findings.title: F00 acceptance does not test Governance Kernel security semantics
findings.description: The frozen F00 contract requires only ROOT_INTEGRITY, STATE_INTEGRITY, PATCH_SCOPE and F00_HELLO_WORLD.
findings.impact: An F00 PASS must never be presented as MGK v0.1.0 FUNCTIONAL=TRUE.
findings.recommended_regression: Use the independent 41-vector corpus and full frozen acceptance for v0.1.0.
findings.rationale: The bootstrap documentation already states this limitation; it is recorded to prevent semantic scope escalation.
